subject: Benchmark methodology exchange: EdgeFin performance SLOs (latency/throughput/concurrency)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Aiden Scott <aiden.scott@edgefin.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — EdgeFin perf SLOs / benchmarking

Thanks for the call today — good to meet the EdgeFin team. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of requirements (from call):
- Target P95 latency: 120ms for 512-token generation (primary).
- Peak throughput target: ~1,500 concurrent requests (avg request size ~350 tokens).
- Target tail latency: P99 < 600ms for single-request case.
- Streaming required for real-time UX (client expects chunked token delivery).
- Preferred model family: open Llama-family variant (we discussed v2-13B quantized options).

Action items we agreed: 
1) Redwood to share benchmark methodology (prompt sets, harness, measurement defs, reproducibility notes).
2) EdgeFin to confirm exact concurrency pattern (burstiness, steady-state) + share representative prompt set if available.
3) Schedule a 1-day replay/benchmark run the week of Nov 9.

Attachments: I’ll upload the initial harness and a sample prompt set in a follow-up email (zipped).

Questions / clarifications:
- Can you confirm whether streaming must preserve per-token latency <40ms? Or is startup latency more important?
- For throughput, do you expect sustained 1,500 qps or short bursts to 1,500 concurrent streams?

Next call: optional sync after you review the harness; otherwise we’ll proceed with scheduling the run.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
(415) 555-0126
From: Aiden Scott <aiden.scott@edgefin.com>

Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — EdgeFin perf SLOs / benchmarking

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick answers and a request from our side: 

Answers: 
- Streaming: preserving per-token latency is important for the editor UX; if per-token delivery can be kept <50ms we’re happy — startup latency can be up to 250ms.
- Concurrency pattern: we expect traffic to be bursty. Typical steady-state concurrency ~400. Peak bursts up to 1,500 concurrent sessions for 30–90s.

Request:
- Can you send the harness and prompt set you mentioned (we’ll attach our sample prompts after we review yours).
- Also share the measurement definitions (how you compute P95/P99, whether you exclude cold-starts, and how streaming latencies are measured).

We’re planning to run the sandbox replay on Nov 10 — will confirm once we ingest your harness.

Thanks,
Aiden Scott
Head of Platform Engineering | EdgeFin
aiden.scott@edgefin.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Aiden Scott <aiden.scott@edgefin.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Benchmark harness + measurement defs (attached)

Thanks Aiden — attaching what we discussed. High-level notes below and reproducibility tips. Attachments: redwood-benchmark-harness-v1.zip, prompt-set-edgefin.csv, measurement-defs.md

What’s in the harness: 
- A replay harness that accepts a CSV of prompts and timestamps and replays them against a specified model endpoint with configurable concurrency and burst profiles.
- Streaming client that records per-token delivery timestamps and aggregates token-level latencies.
- Kernel-level metrics collector (GPU utilization, memory, kernel timings) for correlating infra events.

Measurement definitions (summary):
- P95/P99 for generation latency are computed at the request level from request-start to request-complete (excluding network transfer time outside our controlled harness).
- Streaming per-token latency: measured as token-emission delta from model kernel to first byte returned to client; we record per-token percentiles and 99.9th.
- Cold-start exclusion: we recommend discarding the first 10 requests per worker when computing steady-state percentiles; cold-starts are logged separately.
- Concurrency accounting: concurrency measured as number of in-flight requests at the model runtime; bursts are replayed with the same inter-arrival times from your sample trace to ensure reproducibility.

Reproducibility tips:
- Use the exact model artifacts (we recommend providing the model checksum) and quantization profile.
- Lock worker pool sizes and GPU types when comparing runs.
- We provide a run-config YAML to capture all nondeterministic knobs.

Links: harness + docs are uploaded to the shared Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/EdgeFin/benchmarks/DEAL-3491/harness-v1

Next steps suggested:
1) EdgeFin to drop their representative prompt file (or confirm ours covers the common cases).
2) Confirm benchmark window (Nov 10 works for us — we’ll reserve a dedicated worker pool that day).
3) Redwood to run baseline (no quantization) + quantized run and share a results dashboard.

If you prefer, I can schedule a 30-min walk-through of the harness on Nov 5.

—
Marissa

Aiden — quick clarifying note from infra side: 
- For the burst scenario, can you confirm whether sessions during bursts maintain open streaming connections for the full generation duration, or do you expect many short streaming sessions? We want to size the KV cache and worker concurrency appropriately.
- Also, if you have tokenization variability (some prompts producing much longer outputs), please flag those so we can run headroom tests.

If you’d prefer a short sync with our infra lead (Neha), we can do 20 minutes tomorrow morning.

Thanks
David

Aiden
